description: Quantizer for a scale built from a run of up to 13 intervals, where the run need not add up to an octave

params.text: Chooses the unit the intervals are displayed and typed in: volts, cents, or a frequency ratio shown relative to 1
Sets the interval that EDPO divides into equal chromatic steps, an octave by default and clamped to 4 octaves
Sets how many equal divisions the pseudo-octave is cut into, 12 by default, from 1 to 100
Sets how many intervals the scale runs through before it repeats, 1 to 13, with 12 by default
Sets the note the scale starts from, C4 by default, clamped between C0 and C8
Chooses whether the scale root is displayed and typed as Hz, cents or volts
Sets whether a pitch falling between two scale notes is rounded up, rounded down, or taken to the nearest note
Spreads the notes of the scale over even slices of the whole scale interval, so random input pitches choose each note equally often
Sets that one interval of the scale, in chromatic steps when EQUAL DIVS is on, or as a direct interval of 0 to 2 octaves when it is off
When on, each interval is a number of chromatic steps from dividing the pseudo-octave by EDPO; when off, each interval knob sets its interval directly and PSEUD-OCT INTERVAL and EDPO are ignored

inputs.text: Adds to that interval knob, at 10 chromatic steps per volt when EQUAL DIVS is on, or a volt per octave when it is off
Adds to the PSEUD-OCT INTERVAL knob at a volt per octave, monophonic
Adds to the EDPO knob at 10 divisions per volt, monophonic
Adds to the SCALE LENGTH knob at 0.5V per step, monophonic
Adds to the SCALE ROOT knob at a volt per octave, monophonic
The pitch to be quantized, polyphonic
A trigger patched here quantizes the input pitch on each trigger and holds it in between; unpatched, the quantizing is continuous
Up to 13 channels patched here modulate the 13 interval knobs in turn

outputs.text: A 1ms 10V trigger each time a new note is quantized, or the TRIG input passed through when that is patched
Every note of the scale as pitches, from the scale root through the first note of the next pseudo-octave, one channel per note
A whole-numbered voltage naming the pseudo-octave each quantized note landed in, 0 being the one containing the scale root

menu: Preset — factory presets in five folders of example scales: octave repeating 12ET, non-octave equal divisions, non-octave repeating ratios, cent temperaments, isoharmonic chords
